questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark: KMNP, LNQR, MPRT, NQTU, ?

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Select the related word from the given alternatives. Ampere : Current :: Kelvin : ?
questions.explanation: Ampere is the SI unit of electric current. Similarly, Kelvin is the SI unit of temperature.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Select the related word from the given alternatives. Danube : Europe :: Yangtze : ?
questions.explanation: The Danube River flows through Europe. Similarly, the Yangtze River flows through Asia (China).

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark in the series: DFH, HJL, LNP, PRT, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter in each position shifts +4: D?H?L?P?T, F?J?N?R?V, H?L?P?T?X. So the next term is TVX.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark: ABD, BCF, CDH, DEJ, ?
questions.explanation: Pattern: First letter +1: A?B?C?D?E; Second letter +1: B?C?D?E?F; Third letter +2: D?F?H?J?L. So next term is EFL.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark: CEG, FHJ, ILN, LOQ, ?
questions.explanation: First letter +3: C?F?I?L?O; Second letter +3: E?H?L?O?R; Third letter +3: G?J?N?Q?T. So next term is ORT.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark: ZXVT, YWUS, XVTR, WUSQ, ?
questions.explanation: Each term shifts -1 from the previous term in all positions: Z?Y?X?W?V, X?W?V?U?T, V?U?T?S?R, T?S?R?Q?P. So next term is VTRP.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark: KMPT, LNQU, MORV, NPSW, ?
questions.explanation: First letter +1: K?L?M?N?O; Second letter +1: M?N?O?P?Q; Third letter +1: P?Q?R?S?T; Fourth letter +1: T?U?V?W?X. So next term is OQTX.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: What comes next: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ?
questions.explanation: The pattern is squares of consecutive numbers starting from 2: 2?=4, 3?=9, 4?=16, 5?=25, 6?=36, 7?=49.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: What comes next: 2, 6, 5, 10, 8, 14, 11, ?
questions.explanation: There are two interleaved series: Odd positions: 2,5,8,11 (+3 each); Even positions: 6,10,14,? (+4 each). Next even term = 14+4 = 18.

questions.question: Which of the following addresses are identical to each other? 1. Rohan Sharma, B-204, Palm Residency, Pune, 411001 2. Rohan Sharma, B-204, Palm Residency, Pune, 411001 3. Rohan Sharma, B-204, Palm Residancy, Pune, 411001 4. Rohan S., B-204, Palm Residency, Pune, 411001

questions.question: Find the option that best completes the analogy. BF : JN :: DH : ?

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: A is facing South. B is seated third to the left of A. Who is sitting immediately to the right of B?
options: The person seated to the immediate left of A
The person seated opposite to A
The person seated to the immediate right of A
questions.explanation: We only know B is third to the left of A. We don't know the total number of people, the seating arrangement (circle or line), or who else is present. Hence, it cannot be determined.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: In the following question, the second word is related to the first word by a specific pattern of letter transformation. Apply the same pattern to the third word. LOCK : NQEM :: WORD : ?
questions.explanation: L?N (+2), O?Q (+2), C?E (+2), K?M (+2). So each letter shifts +2. W?Y (+2), O?Q (+2), R?T (+2), D?F (+2) = YQTF.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: In each of the following, a specific pattern such as reversal or rearrangement has been applied to the first word to get the second. Apply the same pattern to the third word. TRAIN : NIART :: CIRCLE : ?
questions.explanation: TRAIN reversed is NIART. Similarly, CIRCLE reversed is ELCRIC.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: In each of the following, the first word is coded to form the second word using a specific rearrangement and/or substitution rule. Apply the same rule to the third word. GARDEN : NEDRAG :: PICTURE : ?
questions.explanation: GARDEN reversed is NEDRAG. Similarly, PICTURE reversed is ERUTCIP.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Identify the odd one: 4, 9, 25, 36, 48, 64
questions.explanation: All numbers except 48 are perfect squares: 2?=4, 3?=9, 5?=25, 6?=36, 8?=64. 48 is not a perfect square.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Which of the following is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: 3,5,7 are consecutive primes; 13,17,19 are primes; 29,31,37 are primes. 2,4,6 are even numbers ? 4 and 6 are not prime numbers, while 2 is prime. So this group does not follow the pattern of all primes.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: Meera said, "The woman in the photo is my father's mother's only daughter-in-law's daughter." Who is the woman to Meera?
questions.explanation: Father's mother = Grandmother. Her only daughter-in-law = Meera's mother. Her daughter = Meera's sister. So the woman is Meera's sister.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: In each of the following, a group of three numbers/symbols is given. Identify the group that does NOT follow the same pattern as the others.
questions.explanation: In a, b, c: Letters go +2 (B?D?F), (C?E?G), (H?J?L) and numbers go +2 (2?4?6), (3?5?7), (8?10?12). In d: Letters go +2 (M?O?Q), but numbers: 13?14 (+1), 14?16 (+2) ? not consistent.

questions.subject: General Intelligence & Reasoning
questions.question: In each of the following, a group of three numbers/symbols is given. Identify the group that does NOT follow the same pattern as the others.
questions.explanation: In a, b, d: Letters go +1 (A?B?C), numbers go +1 (1?2?3), third letters go -1 (Z?Y?X). In c: Letters go +1 (G?H?I), numbers: 7?8 (+1), 8?10 (+2) ? not consistent.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
questions.explanation: Article 32 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Constitutional Remedies. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the "heart and soul" of the Constitution.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which pathway of cellular respiration takes place in the mitochondrial matrix?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Fill in the blank: The classical dance form Mohiniyattam originates from _____.
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form that originates from Kerala, traditionally performed by women.

To guide the module into orbit
To assist docking with a space station

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Santosh Trophy is associated with which sport in India?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which of the following industries falls under the "public sector" classification in India?
options: Owned and operated by government bodies
Owned by workers sharing profits and losses

questions.question: Argon, an inert gas, is primarily produced in the Earth's crust through which process?

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Fundamental Rights and DPSPs is correct?
options: Fundamental Rights are justiciable, but DPSPs are not
Both are equally enforceable by courts
DPSPs override Fundamental Rights in conflict
DPSPs are guaranteed only for citizens
questions.explanation: Fundamental Rights are justiciable (enforceable by courts), while Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) are non-justiciable and act as guidelines for governance.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Under the Global Firepower Military Strength Ranking, which factor is a key parameter assessed?
questions.explanation: The Global Firepower Military Strength Ranking assesses key parameters including defense budget, manpower, air power, naval power, and logistical capabilities.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which Indian classical music tradition uses the term "jaati" to denote the number of beats in a laghu?
questions.explanation: In Carnatic music, the term "jaati" is used to denote the number of beats (laghu) in a tala, with five different jaatis varying from 3 to 9 beats.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Education, after the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, was moved to which list?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) moved education from the State List to the Concurrent List, allowing both the Centre and States to legislate on it.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: What is the average of all integers between 200 and 400 that are exactly divisible by 13?
questions.explanation: Numbers divisible by 13 between 200 and 400: 208, 221, ..., 390. This is an AP with first term 208, last term 390, common difference 13. Average = (208+390)/2 = 598/2 = 299.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The average of 15 numbers is 80. Average of first 6 = 70, next 6 = 20% more than first 6. 13th number is 8 more than 15th; 14th is 4 less than 15th. Find average of 13th and 14th.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A landlord bought a shop for ?12,00,000. He wants a 10% annual return after paying ?3,000/month maintenance. What should be the monthly rent?
questions.explanation: Annual return required = 10% of 12,00,000 = ?1,20,000. Annual maintenance = 3000?12 = ?36,000. Total annual rent required = 1,20,000 + 36,000 = ?1,56,000. Monthly rent = 1,56,000/12 = ?13,000.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: An amount doubles in 4 years with compound interest. How many years will it take to grow to 16 times its original value?
questions.explanation: If amount doubles in 4 years, then 2P = P(1+r/100)? ? (1+r/100)? = 2. For 16P = P(1+r/100)^t ? 16 = 2^t/4. Since 16 = 2?, t/4 = 4 ? t = 16 years.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A sum becomes ?8,000 in 2 years and ?9,600 in 3 years at compound interest. What is the original principal?
questions.explanation: Interest for 3rd year = 9600 - 8000 = ?1,600. This interest is earned on ?8,000 for 1 year, so rate = (1600/8000)?100 = 20% p.a. Amount = P(1.2)? = 8000 ? P = 8000/1.44 = ?5,555.56.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Rakesh purchased 20 L milk at ?40/L and 10 L at ?55/L. He mixed and sold at ?50/L. What was his total profit or loss?

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A retailer marks a refrigerator 60% above CP, offers 20% discount, then 5% festive discount. If final SP is ?18,240, find CP.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A 50-liter mixture contains milk and water in ratio 7:3. How much water must be added to change ratio to 7:5?

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A can complete a task in 12 days, B in 18 days. If they work together for 5 days, what fraction of the work remains?
questions.explanation: A's rate = 1/12, B's rate = 1/18. Together = 1/12+1/18 = (3+2)/36 = 5/36 per day. In 5 days, work done = 5 ? 5/36 = 25/36. Remaining = 1 - 25/36 = 11/36.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Two teas priced at ?80/kg and ?120/kg are blended and sold at ?114/kg, achieving a 14% profit margin. What is the ratio of the two teas in the mixture?

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Three pipes A, B, C fill a tank in 8, 12, 16 hours respectively. All three are opened for 3 hours, then A is closed. How much additional time is needed to fill the tank?

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A superfast train covers a fixed distance in 45 minutes at 200 km/h. Due to diversion, distance increases by 25%. What should its new average speed be to arrive on time?
questions.explanation: Original distance = 200 ? 45/60 = 150 km. New distance = 150 ? 1.25 = 187.5 km. Time = 45 minutes = 0.75 hours. Required speed = 187.5/0.75 = 250 km/h.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Two cars P and Q start from points 400 km apart. Moving towards each other, they meet in 5 hours; moving in same direction, they meet in 20 hours. What is the speed of car P (the faster car)?
questions.explanation: Let speeds be p and q (p > q). Opposite: p+q = 400/5 = 80. Same direction: p?q = 400/20 = 20. Solving: 2p = 100 ? p = 50 km/h.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A circular cake has radius 14 cm. If 60% of it is eaten, what is the area of cake remaining? (Use ?=22/7)

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A ring-shaped disc has outer radius 14 cm and inner radius 7 cm. What is the ratio of the ring's area to the whole outer circle?
questions.explanation: Area of outer circle = ??14? = 196?. Area of inner circle = ??7? = 49?. Ring area = 196? - 49? = 147?. Ratio = 147? : 196? = 147:196 = 3:4.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A car wheel has a radius of 21 cm. What percentage of its circumference is covered in a one-third turn?
questions.explanation: A one-third turn covers 1/3 of the circumference. Percentage = (1/3) ? 100 = 33.33%.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The line y = mx + 7 passes through (2, 15). Find m.
questions.explanation: Substitute x=2, y=15: 15 = m?2 + 7 ? 2m = 8 ? m = 4.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: OBSEQUIOUS
questions.explanation: Obsequious' means excessively obedient or attentive, often to an excessive degree. 'Servile' means having or showing an excessive willingness to serve or please others, which is the closest synonym.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: "A bolt from the blue"
questions.explanation: The idiom 'a bolt from the blue' means a sudden and unexpected event, something that happens without warning, like lightning from a clear blue sky.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word: MUNIFICENT
questions.explanation: Munificent' means extremely generous or lavish in giving. Its antonym is 'miserly', which means extremely stingy or ungenerous.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Identify the misspelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Consensus' (not 'Concensus'). All other options are correctly spelled: Bureaucracy, Occurrence, Questionnaire.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Spot the correct spelling of the medical term for inflammation of the appendix.
questions.explanation: Appendicitis' is the correct spelling for inflammation of the appendix. The other options have common spelling errors such as missing letters or incorrect letter substitutions.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the correct one-word substitute for: 'A person who is unable to sleep'
questions.explanation: An 'insomniac' is a person who suffers from insomnia, i.e., the inability to sleep. A 'somnambulist' is a sleepwalker.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the correct option: The negotiations were so fraught that both sides could ___ finalize the agenda.
questions.explanation: Hardly' means 'barely' or 'only just'. In the context of fraught negotiations, 'could hardly finalize' means they were barely able to finalize the agenda.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the correct option: Rare though the phenomenon is, it can occur ___ extreme temperature fluctuations.
questions.explanation: Under' is the correct preposition to indicate conditions or circumstances. 'Under extreme temperature fluctuations' means in conditions of extreme temperature changes.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the correct option: While the plan appeared feasible on paper, its execution proved ___ challenging than expected.
questions.explanation: More' is the correct comparative form used with 'than'. The sentence contrasts the plan on paper versus its actual execution, indicating greater difficulty than expected.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: That the committee failed to address the core issues (1)/ of the labour dispute were unsurprising (2)/ given the conflicting testimonies (3)/ gathered over multiple sessions. (4)
options: That the committee failed to address the core issues
of the labour dispute were unsurprising
questions.explanation: The error is in part (2). The subject is the entire clause "That the committee failed to address the core issues of the labour dispute," which is singular. Therefore, the verb should be 'was' not 'were'.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: What make the new policy particularly controversial is not its proposed tax structure per se, (1)/ but that it assumes, without adequate evidence, (2)/ a uniformity among regions whose economic conditions are (3)/ vastly incomparable by any objective measure. (4)
options: What make the new policy particularly controversial is not its proposed tax structure per se
but that it assumes, without adequate evidence
a uniformity among regions whose economic conditions are
vastly incomparable by any objective measure
questions.explanation: The error is in part (1). The subject of the verb is 'what' (which is singular in this context). The correct form should be 'What makes', not 'What make'.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Change from active to passive: They have been ignoring the maintenance of the equipment for months.
options: Maintenance of the equipment had been ignored by them for months.
Maintenance of the equipment is being ignored by them for months.
Maintenance of the equipment has been being ignored by them for months.
Maintenance of the equipment was ignored by them for months.
questions.explanation: The active sentence is in Present Perfect Continuous tense ('have been ignoring'). The correct passive form is 'has been being ignored' (though rarely used in practice, it is grammatically correct).

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word: The court adjourned the suit until further evidence was presented.
options: He wore a navy blue suit to the interview.
The suit was filed against the corporation for fraud.
The lawsuit dragged on for over a decade.
The plaintiff's suit was dismissed by the judge.
questions.explanation: The word 'suit' in the given sentence means a legal case. Its homonym is 'suit' meaning a set of clothes, which appears in option A. Options B, C, and D all refer to legal suits.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Convert from passive to active voice: It was being argued by several experts that the strategy had failed internally.
options: Several experts argued that the strategy had failed internally.
The strategy was failing, several experts argued.
The experts were arguing a failed strategy internally.
The strategy had argued failure among several experts.
questions.explanation: The passive sentence 'It was being argued by several experts...' becomes 'Several experts argued that the strategy had failed internally.' in active voice. The tense shifts from Past Continuous Passive to Simple Past Active.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Read the passage and answer: What is the primary trade-off discussed in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly discusses the trade-off between efficiency and resilience, stating that they are complementary virtues with an inherent tension between them.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: What event is cited as an example of over-optimized systems failing?
questions.explanation: The passage cites the COVID-19 pandemic as the event where globally optimized supply chains buckled under sudden demand shifts, illustrating the failure of over-optimized systems.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Why is resilience harder to quantify than efficiency?
options: Its value is realized only during crises, not routine operations
It is a subjective term with no clear definition
questions.explanation: The passage states that resilience is harder to quantify 'since its value is realized only in moments of crisis, not routine operation.'

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: What does the author suggest organizations should do?
options: Recalibrate the balance between efficiency and resilience
questions.explanation: The author suggests that organizations should 'recalibrate the balance' between efficiency and resilience, not abandoning efficiency completely.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: What is meant by "strategic redundancy" in the passage?
options: Deliberate buffers and backups to withstand disruption
questions.explanation: The passage defines 'strategic redundancy' as buffers, backups, and diversified supply chains that help withstand disruption, not unnecessary duplication.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part: He has the reputation to be a ruthless negotiator.
questions.explanation: The correct phrase is 'reputation of being'. Option B, 'of being a ruthless negotiator', correctly replaces the highlighted part and maintains the intended meaning.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part: The mentor advised her to avoid procrastinating and doing her tasks on time.
options: to avoid procrastinating and to do her tasks on time
avoiding procrastination and doing tasks on time
to not procrastinate and do tasks on time
to avoid procrastination and to doing tasks on time
questions.explanation: For parallel structure, 'to avoid' should be followed by 'to do'. Option A maintains proper parallelism: 'to avoid procrastinating and to do her tasks on time'.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Convert to indirect speech: She asked me, "Where have you kept the documents?"
options: She asked me where I had kept the documents.
She asked me where have I kept the documents.
She asked me where I have kept the documents.
She asked me where had I kept the documents.
questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the interrogative sentence changes to an affirmative sentence. 'Have you kept' changes to 'I had kept' (Past Perfect), and the question word 'where' remains.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Convert to direct speech: He said that he would submit the report by evening.
options: I will submit the report by evening, he said.
I would submit the report by evening, he said.
I shall submit the report by evening, he said.
I can submit the report by evening, he said.
questions.explanation: In direct speech, 'would' becomes 'will'. Therefore, the direct speech is: "I will submit the report by evening," he said.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Rearrange the sentences to make a logical passage: The final report was compiled after cross-verification. Field surveys were conducted across multiple districts. Raw data was entered into a centralized database. Researchers identified target regions for the study.
questions.explanation: The logical order is: Researchers identified target regions (4), then conducted field surveys (2), then entered raw data (3), and finally compiled the report (1). So the order is 4-2-3-1.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph: It typically involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting numerical data. Statistics is a branch of mathematics dealing with data collection and analysis. This can be either descriptive, summarizing data, or inferential, drawing conclusions. The insights derived are then used to inform decision-making across various fields.
questions.explanation: The logical order is: 2 (introduces Statistics), 1 (describes what it involves), 3 (explains the two types), and 4 (concludes with its application). So the order is 2, 1, 3, 4.
